title: Bone Stress Injury Epidemiology and Risk Factors in Female Off-Road Runners: A Systematic Review
authors: Stennett R, Scheer V, Kaulback K
population: Female off-road (trail and cross-country) runners; 17 studies, 897 female runners
findings: 17 studies included (searches to July 2024); only 2 reported risk factors for BSI.
BSI incidence ranged from 0 to 34.39 per 100,000 athlete-exposures and prevalence from 0% to 40.9%; most BSIs were high severity and in the lower leg.
Eight significant intrinsic risk factors: increasing age, disrupted menstruation, previous BSI, increased female triad risk, and lower calcium, vitamin D and calorie intake.
Authors note scarcity of data and call for high-quality prospective studies.
limitations: Systematic review without meta-analysis; scarce data on the target population, cross-country runners included, only 2 studies on risk factors.
implications: Supports counting previous BSI, menstrual disruption, triad/REDs risk and low intake as BSI risk-flag factors for female trail runners.
Age was a risk factor here, so do not restrict BSI vigilance to young athletes.

verification.notes: Added by verifier. Crossref (J Sport Rehabil, 2025-07, first author Stennett) matches; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 39874957) supports all findings.
